A1.justification: Both PDFs describe InfAlign and are readable, including their figures, equations, and appendices. Corresponding content can be matched despite substantial rewriting, reorganization, and experimental revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original PaLM-2 alignment experiments on Anthropic helpfulness and harmlessness, calibration ablations, and reward-hacking experiments.

after.justification: v3 reports original alignment experiments on Anthropic helpfulness, harmlessness, and Reddit summarization, together with the retained reward-hacking experiment.

M1.justification: v1's practical algorithm uses median-based logarithmic calibration, with a multiple-anchor extension in Appendix D. v3 Algorithm 1 instead uses empirical rank calibration through Equation (12), including half credit for reward ties. This replaces a central calibration component while retaining reward transformation and KL-regularized RL. However, v3 Section 5.5 still mentions median calibration.

E1.justification: v3 adds Reddit TL;DR summarization for policy and reward-model training and for standard and Best-of-N evaluation. This extends coverage beyond v1's Anthropic helpfulness and harmlessness dialogue tasks to a distinct summarization task.

E2.justification: v1 Figures 3, 4, and 7 include a separate Best-Of-N comparator; v3 Figures 4 and 6 drop that entry and include Wang et al.'s log-sigmoid reward transformation. BoND, BoNBoN, and IPO were already evaluated in v1, and uncalibrated is relabeled PPO. The duplicate IPO entry in v3's standard harmlessness panel makes that panel's green comparator ambiguous.

E3.justification: The miscalibration check changes its stated source from 10 training prompts in v1 Section 6.2 to 10 test prompts in v3 Section 5.2; this does not establish that it was rerun. Real-model evaluations no longer report N=2, while N=4 and N=32 remain. The principal model families, Anthropic training counts, and KL-regularization grid are retained.

E4.justification: v3 removes the calibration-error CDF comparison and the rollout-count and anchor-count ablations in v1 Figure 2 and Appendix D.1/Figure 5. It also reduces the exponential-transformation variants shown in empirical and analytical comparisons. These substantially narrow calibration and sensitivity analysis. The poisoning experiment and much of the analytical comparison are retained in v3 Appendices D and F.

E5.justification: v3 Figures 4 and 6 add shaded bands around empirical win-rate curves, whereas the corresponding v1 plots show lines and markers without bands. Their statistical meaning, confidence level, and construction are unspecified. Neither PDF supplies repeated-run or seed counts, so the bands do not establish additional runs.

E6.justification: v3 adds summarization results and revises the Anthropic curves and rankings, while removing empirical N=2 and several transformation results. Sections 5.4–5.5 report gains up to 3% for helpfulness, 8% for summarization, and 5% for harmlessness against the best baseline. v1 Sections 6.4–6.5 report 8–12% and 4–9% against uncalibrated models. These are revised comparisons, not directly comparable performance gains or losses between versions.

T1.justification: The central theoretical framework is retained. v3 adds a finite-sample calibration bound in Lemma 6 and a BoN/WoN density proof in Appendix B.6, and corrects a missing factor in the Corollary 2 derivation and the reward-loss sign in Appendix C. There are also new inconsistencies: Equation (4) omits the reward expectation, and the new density proof omits the normalization factor N stated in Lemma 5.

C1.justification: The central claim that inference-aware alignment can be expressed through transformed-reward RLHF remains. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion broaden the empirical contribution to summarization and revise the advertised improvement range to 3–8%, changing the scope and magnitude of the empirical claim.

C2.justification: v1 attributes standard-win-rate gains to estimating win rates more efficiently using multiple reference samples rather than existing pairwise data. v3 instead emphasizes calibration robustness and reduced reward hacking. It removes the qualification that the retained poisoning experiment used a different, pointwise-loss calibration, making that experiment's support for the proposed procedure less clearly qualified.

D1.justification: v3 explicitly sets K=100 as the experimental calibration default; v1 discussed 100 samples alongside its median-calibration ablations, so this does not establish increased sampling. v3 removes the full PaLM-XL judging prompt from v1 Appendix C and the pointwise-loss disclosure for the poisoning experiment. These are limited but relevant reproducibility changes.

R1.justification: Most related-work discussion is retained. v3 adds a substantive comparison with Chow et al.'s inference-aware BoN fine-tuning, distinguishing binary rewards and absence of KL regularization. It also adds references including DeepSeek-R1, constrained generation, and the DKW inequality, while removing the Xie et al. reasoning-calibration reference.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, and the contribution bullets become a narrative with an organization paragraph. The theoretical and practical method sections are integrated, related work moves to Appendix A, and the conclusion loses its future-work paragraph while acknowledgment and impact statements are added. This substantially changes the document's narrative structure.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout. v3 adds the framework diagram, combines standard and inference-time results into the six-panel Figure 4, redraws analytical plots and moves their full comparison to Appendix F, and removes calibration diagnostic displays. The retained poisoning figure is relocated and enlarged.

improvement.justification: v3 improves the connection between practical calibration and theory through empirical calibration with a finite-sample bound, and tests transfer beyond dialogue on summarization. The reorganized explanation also helps. The net gain is limited by removed sensitivity evidence and calibration disclosures, residual median-calibration wording in Section 5.5, and new mathematical inconsistencies in Equation (4) and Appendix B.6.
